w: Built in the 1560s over a 10th-century fortress for Archduke Ferdinand II, this Renaissance castle above Innsbruck housed his wife Philippine Welser and one of history's great art collections. Its Lower Castle, purpose-built as a museum, still holds Ferdinand's original Kunstkammer -- among the oldest museums in the world -- plus armouries spanning Maximilian I to Leopold I.
s: Habsburg archduke's castle holds the original Kunstkammer
_facts: Renaissance castle at 632m, built 16th c. over a 10th-c. fortress
Home of Archduke Ferdinand II 1567-1595, built for wife Philippine Welser
Lower Castle museum holds original Kunstkammer, among oldest museums in the world
Armouries span Emperor Maximilian I to Emperor Leopold I; Spanish Hall above

w: One of Austria's three most significant historic buildings, alongside Vienna's Hofburg and Schonbrunn, this former Habsburg palace began under Archduke Sigismund around 1460, absorbing stretches of the old city wall. Empress Maria Theresa rebuilt it in Baroque style from 1754, adding the Giants' Hall with Maulbertsch ceiling frescoes and an Imperial Chapel completed in 1765.
s: Habsburg palace rebuilt in Baroque by Maria Theresa
_facts: Former Habsburg palace, begun c.1460 under Archduke Sigismund
Rebuilt in Baroque style 1754-1773 under Empress Maria Theresa
Giants' Hall has ceiling frescoes by Franz Anton Maulbertsch
Complex includes the Hofkirche, Silver Chapel and Innsbruck Cathedral

w: First jumped from simple wooden ramps in the 1920s, this hill was rebuilt for the 1964 Winter Olympics and again for 1976, then remade entirely in 2003 to a design by Zaha Hadid. Its 26,000-capacity stadium hosts the third leg of the Four Hills Tournament every January, one of ski jumping's most prestigious fixtures.
s: Zaha Hadid's ski jump hosts the Four Hills Tournament
_facts: First competitions in the 1920s on wooden ramps
Rebuilt for the 1964 and 1976 Winter Olympics
Current hill (2003) designed by Zaha Hadid
Hosts third leg of Four Hills Tournament; stadium capacity 26,000

w: Built 1717-1724 on the site of a 12th-century Romanesque church, this Baroque cathedral -- decorated in part by the Asam brothers -- holds two treasures: Lucas Cranach the Elder's Maria Hilf, among Christendom's most venerated Marian images, and the canopied tomb of Archduke Maximilian III. Heavily damaged in the Second World War, it was fully restored within a few years.
s: Baroque cathedral holding a venerated Cranach Madonna
_facts: Built 1717-1724 by Johann Jakob Herkomer, replacing a 12th-c. church
Interior decoration in part by the Asam brothers
Houses Lucas Cranach the Elder's Maria Hilf, c.1530
Tomb of Archduke Maximilian III; heavily damaged in WWII, fully restored

w: The southernmost chain of the Karwendel range rises straight from Innsbruck's northern edge, its highest point the 2,637m Kleiner Solstein. The Nordkette Cable Car climbs to Hafelekar station at 2,269m, gateway to the Innsbruck Klettersteig via ferrata running west via Seegrube and Frau Hitt, while below, the Nordkette Singletrail ranks among Europe's toughest freeride mountain-bike routes.
s: Cable car climbs straight from the city to a via ferrata
_facts: Southernmost range of the Karwendel; highest point Kleiner Solstein, 2,637m
Nordkette Cable Car reaches Hafelekar station at 2,269m
Starting point of the Innsbruck Klettersteig via ferrata
Nordkette Singletrail is a noted freeride mountain-bike descent

w: Built in 1553 as Emperor Ferdinand I's memorial to his grandfather Maximilian I, this Gothic church holds a cenotaph surrounded by a remarkable collection of German Renaissance sculpture -- Maximilian is actually buried at Wiener Neustadt, where his planned tomb was never built. The church also holds the tomb of Andreas Hofer, Tyrol's national hero.
s: Gothic church built as a cenotaph for Maximilian I
_facts: Built 1553 by Ferdinand I as a memorial to Maximilian I
Maximilian's cenotaph surrounded by German Renaissance sculpture
Maximilian is actually buried at Wiener Neustadt
Holds the tomb of Andreas Hofer, Tyrol's national hero

w: A modest 746m hill where the Sill meets the Inn valley, used since the Iron Age as a cremation site and settlement. In 1809 it was the site of four battles led by the Tyrolean freedom fighter Andreas Hofer; an 1892 monument commemorates them. The Brenner railway and motorway both tunnel beneath it, and the Sill Gorge sits at its base.
s: Hill where Andreas Hofer fought four battles in 1809
_facts: 746m hill at the Sill-Inn confluence; Iron Age cremation site
Site of the four Battles of Bergisel, 1809, led by Andreas Hofer
Andreas Hofer monument erected 1892
Brenner railway and Brennerautobahn tunnel beneath it; Sill Gorge at its base

w: Housed in four wings of a former Franciscan monastery around an arcaded Renaissance courtyard, this is Tyrol's foremost collection of regional handicrafts, costumes and folk art. Restored wood-paneled rooms rescued from historic farms and noble houses span the Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque periods, alongside a collection of carved and wax Nativity mangers dating to the 18th century.
s: Tyrol's folk art collection in a former monastery
_facts: Housed in a former Franciscan monastery, arcaded Renaissance courtyard
Most important collection of Tyrolean cultural artifacts
Restored Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque wood-paneled rooms from historic farms
Extensive Nativity manger collection dating to the 18th century

w: A highland fen lake 2.5km west of Natters at 830m, ringed by hiking trails and reed beds that feed it fresh water through pipes. Despite being fen-fed, it holds Grade A water quality and supports several kinds of carp, with summer temperatures reaching 18-20C -- one of the larger highland lakes near Innsbruck.
s: Grade-A highland lake above Innsbruck, stocked with carp
_facts: 830m elevation, 2.5km west of Natters
Fen water lake, still Grade A water quality
Several carp species live in the lake
Summer water temperature 18-20C

w: A listed equestrian monument on the Rennweg near the Tyrolean State Theatre in Innsbruck's Altstadt. The fountain -- Leopoldsbrunnen -- takes its name from the bronze rider astride it, Archduke Leopold V, who lived from 1586 to 1632. One of the quieter Habsburg-era monuments scattered through the old city centre.
s: Equestrian fountain honouring Archduke Leopold V
_facts: Listed monument on the Rennweg, near the Altstadt
Equestrian statue of Archduke Leopold V (1586-1632)
Fountain named Leopoldsbrunnen after him

w: A monument on Eduard-Wallnofer-Platz in central Innsbruck, erected in 1997 to commemorate the November pogroms of 1938, during which the Innsbruck citizens Josef Adler, Wilhelm Bauer, Richard Berger and Richard Graubart were murdered. A deliberate, unshowy marker of that night placed in the city's own civic square.
s: Memorial to four Jews murdered in Innsbruck's 1938 pogrom
_facts: Located on Eduard-Wallnofer-Platz, central Innsbruck
Commemorates the November pogroms of 1938
Names four murdered Innsbruck citizens: Adler, Bauer, Berger, Graubart
Erected 1997

w: A traditional inn in the heart of Innsbruck's historic centre, sheltering merchants and travellers on the road between Italy and Germany since its founding in 1390. Six centuries on, the Goldener Adler still trades on that same reputation for rest and shelter to those passing through the Alps.
_facts: Traditional inn in Innsbruck's historic centre
Founded 1390
Historically served merchants and travellers between Italy and Germany

w: Tucked inside the Hofburg, this museum run by the Austrian Alpine Club (OAV) is devoted to the history of alpinism. Assessed as 'excellent' for both the Tyrolean and Austrian Museum Prizes in 2009, it was also nominated for the European Museum Prize the following year.
s: Museum inside the Hofburg tracing alpinism's history
_facts: Located in the Hofburg, Altstadt
Owned by the Austrian Alpine Club (OAV)
Dedicated to the history of alpinism
Rated 'excellent' for Tyrolean/Austrian Museum Prizes 2009; nominated for European Museum Prize 2010

w: In Igls, southeast of the city, this bobsleigh, luge and skeleton track was rebuilt in 1975 as the first permanent, artificially refrigerated combination track of its kind anywhere -- a model copied by tracks worldwide ever since. It hosted the bobsleigh, luge and skeleton events of the 2012 Winter Youth Olympics.
s: First-of-its-kind refrigerated bobsled and luge track
_facts: Located in Igls, southeast of Innsbruck
Current track completed 1975
First permanent artificially refrigerated combination bobsleigh/luge/skeleton track
Hosted 2012 Winter Youth Olympics sliding events
